entities.summary: Ma Shi, courtesy name Jingzhan (敬瞻), was a Chinese landscape painter, court astronomer, and poet during the Xuande era of the early Ming dynasty. His work was heavily influenced by the teachings of the Confucian scholar, Wang Xizhi (, 303–361 CE), who was a prominent figure in the development of Chinese landscape painting. Ma Shi's most famous works include his 'Garden of the Azure Spring' and 'Garden of the Golden Pavilion,' which were commissioned by the Ming dynasty court. These paintings showcased Ma Shi's mastery of traditional Chinese landscape painting techniques, such as the use of ink and brushwork, and his ability to capture the serene beauty of nature. The paintings were highly regarded by the royal family and were often displayed in the imperial palace. Ma Shi's work had a significant impact on the development of Chinese landscape painting, and his paintings continue to be celebrated for their beauty and technical skill. Ma Shi was a native of Jiading, and his exact birth and death years are unknown. His legacy as a leading figure in Chinese landscape painting has endured for centuries, and his work remains highly prized by collectors and scholars today.
